summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Copperline Health through the Console: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost decomposition. Discussed traffic tagging, route-level chargeback, and tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated/private deployments for latency, cost, and compliance. Security questions (SOC2, KMS, VPC) surfaced; agreed on sandbox benchmarking and follow-up security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Copperline - Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Copperline - CTO), Nina Gomez (Copperline - Security)

[00:00:00] Lina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 55 minutes, so we'll do a quick intro then jump into the Console, show usage lenses, per route dashboards, and then the cost break down and Q&A. Marcus will run the demo.
[00:00:18] Asha: Great, thanks Lina. We're excited — quick context, our main ask is to get a pilot for customer-facing summarization routes, want to understand per-route spend and latency headroom.
[00:00:33] Marcus: Perfect. Before I share screen, quick qualifying q: expected QPS on the summarization route and avg prompt size?
[00:00:40] Tom: We're estimating 12 rps at peak for the pilot, prompt lengths vary between 200-800 tokens; we care about p95 latency under 350ms if possible.
[00:00:56] Marcus: Good, that's totally in scope for both hosted and dedicated but tradeoffs apply. Ok sharing screen — you should see the Console home, usage summary. Apologies if the nav labels are fuzzy — connection is a bit choppy.
[00:01:20] [screen shows Usage Overview -> last 7 days chart]
[00:01:25] Marcus: Top left is total tokens and calls; we've got token burn and call counts line charts, below that a breakdown by route — you'll notice each route can be tagged with application, environment, and customer-id.
[00:01:44] Asha: That's nice. How are routes detected? We already have service-level routing on our side.
[00:01:52] Marcus: You can set the route identifier in the request header (x-redwood-route), or map by API key. For your pilot we'll recommend client-side tagging so you get consistent per-route metrics.
[00:02:10] Nina: On data privacy — if we send PII in prompts, what's retained?
[00:02:16] Lina: Quick answer: hosted default retention is 30 days for logs, with an opt-out flag for no retention. For enterprise contracts we can set retention policy or dedicated/private deployment where logs stay in your VPC. We'll follow up with the security doc.
[00:02:34] Marcus: Back to the dashboard — click route 'summarizer-api' — now we see per-route token histogram, latency percentiles, and cost stack. The cost view attributes spend across model, GPU-hours, and network.
[00:02:54] [00:03:01] Marcus: Notice the 'Cost per call' metric — it's token-weighted and includes a model factor and infra factor. You can filter by model variant, e.g., open-7B-quant vs open-13B-fp16.
[00:03:18] Tom: Can we do per-customer chargeback? e.g., user-level usage in the same route?
[00:03:24] Marcus: Yes — we'll show you the 'slice' tab next — you can add dimensions like customer_id and the Console will break down cost per slice, and export CSV for billing. There's a mapping UI to convert attributes into billing buckets.
[00:03:45] Asha: How accurate is the cost model — we have finance people who will want to reconcile.
[00:03:51] Lina: The Console uses token accounting plus infra attribution from node telemetry. It's within expected variance — usually within 5-10% of raw infra cost depending on caching and burst behavior. We also provide a raw export of execution traces for reconciliation.
[00:04:10] [00:04:20] Marcus: Now walking through prefetched cache and KV cache signals — prefix caching reduces token cost for repeated prefixes, and KV cache shows cache hits/evictions. For your summarization route, we usually see 8-12% token reduction from prefix caching with conversational patterns.
[00:04:39] Nina: If we go dedicated, can we enable on-prem KMS for keys?
[00:04:44] Marcus: Yes, Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM; we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP CMEK. For on-prem we support HSM endpoints.
[00:04:58] [00:05:12] Marcus: Next: model variants panel — you can create rollouts, canary tests, and automatic fallback policies. For example, route can try open-13B-fp16 and on failure route to open-7B-quant. This is helpful for graceful degradation under capacity pressure.
[00:05:32] Tom: How does fallback affect latency? We need consistent SLOs.
[00:05:36] Marcus: Fallback will add added latency only when model fails; our routing has a latency-aware policy you can set per-route. If p95 is critical we recommend dedicated with pinned models.
[00:05:50] [00:06:02] Asha: About batching — what's the tradeoff? We need low p95 but also low cost.
[00:06:08] Marcus: Batching increases throughput and lowers per-token cost but increases tail latency. In the Console Optimize tab we give suggestions — e.g., at 12 rps with 200-800 tokens, small batching window (20-40ms) can slash unit cost by ~20% with minimal p95 impact. We'll run a sandbox test to tune.
[00:06:30] [00:06:40] Lina: Quick commercial note — hosted is fastest to ship; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation. For your pilot if latency is strict and you want no noisy neighbors, Dedicated is recommended.
[00:06:55] Tom: Pricing — are there committed discounts?
[00:06:59] Lina: Yes, Dedicated has reserved capacity commitments with discounts. I'll share a side-by-side hosted vs dedicated cost model after the call.
[00:07:12] [00:07:30] Marcus: Now opening the Audit Logs page — shows per-token traces, request headers, and model response times. You can set retention and export to your SIEM via S3 or direct syslog.
[00:07:45] Nina: We need audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance and need proof of encryption in transit/storage for SOC2.
[00:07:53] Lina: We support encrypted transfer (TLS 1.2/1.3) and server-side encryption for S3 exports; we'll include the KMS integration details in the security packet.
[00:08:08] [00:08:20] Marcus: Switching to chargeback reports — you can generate per-route monthly reports and align them with your internal finance codes. There's an API to pull these and push into your billing pipeline.
[00:08:36] Asha: Can we tag routes automatically from service mesh? We use Istio.
[00:08:41] Marcus: Yes you can map Istio attributes to route tags via our ingestion layer; we have an ingestion adapter doc (I'll send link).
[00:08:55] [00:09:10] Marcus: I'm going to simulate a traffic spike so you can see autoscaling and behavior in charts. Spike in 3...2...1.
[00:09:18] [graphs update showing CPU, GPU utilization, queue length]
[00:09:22] Marcus: During the spike you can see autoscaling triggers — we have burst capacity controls and max scaling policies. The Console highlights when fallbacks engaged.
[00:09:36] Tom: What's burst capacity cost like?
[00:09:40] Lina: Burst uses on-demand capacity billed at a premium; we show estimated cost in the Console under the scenario planner. You can cap burst to control spend.
[00:09:55] [00:10:10] Nina: About data residency — pilot customers in EU need data to stay in EU, can Redwood pin region?
[00:10:17] Marcus: Yes, you can pin routes or tenants to regions. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy in your cloud region. For hosted, we have region controls for data locality commitments.
[00:10:35] Asha: Ok nice. On the Console, is there a way to compare model accuracy vs spend for an eval set?
[00:10:42] Marcus: Yes under Optimize -> Eval you can run prompt sets across model variants and see quality metrics vs cost per call. That helps pick an economic frontier.
[00:10:58] [00:11:10] Marcus: Example: here's a QA dataset run — blue line is ROUGE, orange is cost per call. You pick the Pareto point balancing cost and quality.
[00:11:23] Asha: We'll definitely want that for our clinical summary accuracy checks.
[00:11:28] Nina: We'll need an audit trail of eval runs for compliance.
[00:11:32] Marcus: Eval runs are logged and exportable; they include model versions, seed prompts, and outputs.
[00:11:44] [00:12:00] Marcus: Now the sandbox — I'll create a tenant named copperline-pilot and pre-load a sample workload. Give me dev access?
[00:12:08] Asha: Yes send Marcus my email asha@copperline.ai.
[00:12:12] Marcus: Got it, will invite.
[00:12:18] Lina: A couple of gotchas to call out — (1) quantized models reduce memory but may slightly change outputs; (2) caching can affect evaluation if not accounted for; (3) prefix caching works best with repeated system prompts.
[00:12:35] Tom: On quantization, we can't have subtle drift in clinical summarization. How do you mitigate that?
[00:12:41] Marcus: We run regression evals. Optimize suggests model + quantization combos that pass your baseline eval. For strict accuracy we recommend fp16 variants or dedicated pinned fp16 models.
[00:12:56] [00:13:10] Asha: What about costs for KV cache storage?
[00:13:14] Marcus: KV cache is memory-backed on the serving nodes; cost appears as infra-memory in the cost stack. Typically minor vs model compute but depends on cache size and retention.
[00:13:30] Nina: For private deployment, what's the upgrade/patch process?
[00:13:36] Marcus: Private comes with a control plane that you can manage; we provide patch releases and can coordinate rolling upgrades during maintenance windows. Everything is backward compatible for config.
[00:13:49] [00:14:00] Marcus: Jumping to the 'Alerting' section — you can set cost thresholds per route and get emailed or webhook notifications. Example: if route monthly spend exceeds $5k fire a webhook to Slack.
[00:14:15] Asha: Perfect, we need that to keep finance in the loop.
[00:14:19] Tom: For the pilot timeline, we want to be live early Jan. Is that feasible?
[00:14:25] Lina: Yes — action items are lightweight: sandbox +benchmarks this month, security questionnaire and SOC2 scope, then a short pilot contract for Jan.
[00:14:36] [00:14:50] Marcus: I'll demonstrate exporting a per-route CSV — you can see call count, token count, cost breakdown, tags. You can import that into your billing tool and allocate to teams.
[00:15:06] Nina: Will the CSV include model version and quantization flags?
[00:15:10] Marcus: Yes, metadata columns include model_version, quantized:true/false, node_region.
[00:15:21] [00:15:40] Asha: Any compliance red flags we should know?
[00:15:45] Lina: Nothing unusual. For clinical data the biggest ask is tenancy isolation and auditability; Dedicated or Private is common. We'll provide a compliance pack.
[00:15:56] Tom: On SLAs, we need 99.9% uptime for the pilot — is that standard?
[00:16:04] Lina: Dedicated has SLA options; hosted has an SLA for paid tiers. We'll include details in the follow-up doc.
[00:16:15] [00:16:30] Marcus: Now a quick walk through the 'Scenario Planner' — you can model cost by traffic patterns, model mix, and caching ratios. This helps forecast monthly spend.
[00:16:44] Asha: Could you run our expected pattern? 12 rps peak, 60% small prompts, 40% long.
[00:16:52] Marcus: I'll save that scenario and run — result shows estimated monthly cost and breakdown. I'm toggling dedicated pricing vs hosted, you'll see difference.
[00:17:06] [00:17:20] Marcus: Hosted estimated $X/month, Dedicated baseline committed capacity $Y/month with discount after commit. I'll attach the numbers in a spreadsheet.
[00:17:34] Tom: We'll need the spreadsheet for finance.
[00:17:37] Lina: I'll send that after the call; it's one of the next steps.
[00:17:45] [00:17:55] Nina: Can Redwood guarantee data deletion post-retention if requested?
[00:18:00] Marcus: Yes. For enterprise we include data deletion APIs and can purge logs/objects on request; for Private your admin can run deletion themselves.
[00:18:12] Asha: Anything else on the Console that we should explore?
[00:18:17] Marcus: There's a policies engine — you can set per-route SLOs, auto-fallback, and cost caps. Also a Drift Monitoring that alerts when model outputs change beyond thresholds.
[00:18:32] Asha: Drift monitoring sounds useful. We need to track hallucination rate over time.
[00:18:37] Marcus: We support custom metrics for that and hook into your eval pipelines.
[00:18:48] [00:19:00] Lina: Ok wrapping toward next steps. Recap: Marcus will spin up sandbox for Copperline, populate sample workload and run perf/accuracy benchmarks; Lina to send pricing and contract summary; Nina to send security questionnaire responses.
[00:19:15] Tom: Sounds good. Do we want another call after sandbox results?
[00:19:19] Lina: Yes, propose a bench review on Dec 16 — Marcus and Asha to attend.
[00:19:25] Asha: Dec 16 works for me.
[00:19:30] Nina: I'll review the security packet once received.
[00:19:33] [00:19:45] Marcus: Quick note — I'll include a step-by-step for tagging and the Istio adapter link.
[00:19:50] Lina: Thanks everyone. Any final quick q's?
[00:19:55] Tom: No, that's it.
[00:20:00] Lina: Great, thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and the docs.
[00:20:05] [end of demo portion — remaining minutes were clarifying questions and loose scheduling, recorded as short notes]
[00:30:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[00:35:00] Speaker 2: yeah uh hm
[00:45:00] Marcus: reiterating sandbox invite will go out today, will set up perf scripts.
[00:50:00] Asha: thanks, appreciate it.
[00:56:00] Lina: We are ending the call now. Bye.

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-attribution and minor transcription errors expected; names sometimes shortened to first name only.
